script.title: C Pointers: Address and Dereference

sections.heading: Pointer basics
sections.explanation: A pointer is a variable that stores the memory address of another object. The pointer's type describes the kind of object it points to.
sections.example: If an integer variable x is stored at address 1000, an int pointer can store 1000.

sections.heading: Address and dereference
sections.explanation: The address-of operator & obtains an object's address. The unary * operator dereferences a pointer to access the object at that address.
sections.example: If p stores the address of x, *p reads x and assigning to *p changes x.

keyTakeaways: A pointer stores an address, not the pointed-to value itself.
&x obtains x's address; *p accesses the object p points to.
